terra.problem: The cookie comparison has no discernible twist: biting a cookie is ordinary, so it does not convey the warning about a pleasing appearance followed by bitterness.
It guesses why the baker chose the answer and what that says about the baker’s heart, neither of which Papa knows.
The father describes where the woman’s feet go; he does not send her anywhere.
The text says she does not consider the path of life. It does not say she is not weighing where her own road goes.
The claim that a man’s years are all he has goes beyond the text, which also mentions vigor.
The quotation uses “I” without first identifying the speaker as the son in the father’s warning.
The reply-all comparison turns the brink of utter ruin into an embarrassing message sent by mistake. The actions do not match, and the comparison diminishes the serious warning.
